verdict_check.mapping_applied: Conjecture falsification criteria: refuted if (L2-L0) <= 0.0 pp; supported if P1 and P2 and P4 all pass AND P3 passes or is underpowered AND P5 passes; revised otherwise. My recomputed values: L2-L0 = +13.913 pp (not refuted); P1 = pass (13.913 >= 5.0); P2 = fail (85.2174 < 93.0435); P3 = underpowered (n = 0 < 25, not adjudicated); P4 = pass (193.7 <= 15000 and added query 147.4 recorded / 148.2 recomputed, both <= 500); P5 = pass (+5.217 >= 0.0). P1 passes with an adjudicated secondary failing, so the mapping yields revised. adjudicate_c36.py transcribes all five frozen thresholds faithfully (P1_MIN_PP 5.0, P3_MIN_PP 8.0, P3_MIN_N 25, P4_BUILD_MS 15000, P4_QUERY_MS 500) and its branch order matches the conjecture's clause order; its assertion that L0 and L2 share a denominator holds (115 = 115).

defects.detail: P4's added per-query figure (147.4 ms) is not reproducible from localization.jsonl under any estimator I tested. The difference of per-arm medians is 147.5 ms (L2 256.2 - L0 108.7, both of which reproduce exactly from the raw wall_ms) and the median of the 115 paired per-question differences is 148.2 ms. metrics-c36.json states added_ms_L2_vs_L0_median = 147.4 alongside per_query_ms_median values that internally imply 147.5. The label 'median' is also ambiguous between the two estimators, which differ by 0.7 ms here. Immaterial to P4 (the threshold is 500 ms, a 3.4x margin) and to the verdict, but it is a number in the results table that does not come out of the records.

The registration's §5 measures list is not fully delivered and the shortfall is nowhere disclosed. 'Marginal tokens' per arm appears in no record (the p5 records carry prompt_chars and read_events, no token fields); 'peak RSS' for index build is absent from metrics-c36.json; and the 'cross-language subset' measurement — which registration §2 explicitly says can fire the D3 trigger for a successor — is neither computed nor recorded as not-computed. The results document discloses the P3 emptiness and the 115-vs-120 denominator but is silent on these three registered measures.

The results document reports arm differences with no uncertainty statement of any kind, on a paired design where it is cheap. My exact McNemar tests on the paired records: P1 (L2 vs L0) 17 vs 1 discordant, p = 0.00014; P2 (L2 vs L1) 2 vs 11, p = 0.0225; L1 vs L0 28 vs 3, p < 1e-5. But the document's narrative claim 3, that the implementation 'adds a real but modest margin' over FTS5 (+3.4 pp), rests on 5 vs 1 discordant pairs, p = 0.219 — the one headline comparison that the records do not support as distinguishable from noise, asserted as 'real' without qualification. Likewise P5's +5.2 pp is 14 vs 8 discordant, p = 0.286; the document calls it a PASS (which it is, the threshold is directional Δ >= 0) but the surrounding prose treats it as an established gain.

The results document's claim 4 states the downstream accuracy gain 'is fully accounted for by localization'. Decomposing the +5.217 pp into a localization component (+7.47 pp, from 82/115 to 98/115 located at L0's conditional rates) and a conditional-accuracy component (-2.25 pp, since accuracy given located FALLS from 53.66% to 50.00%) shows the gain is localization-driven and partly offset by a conditional-accuracy decline. 'Fully accounted for' understates that L2's answering is worse on the documents it does locate. The document reports both conditional numbers honestly one sentence earlier, so this is an interpretive overreach rather than a hidden number.

The premature-adjudication incident is disclosed in prose but is not checkable from the attached records: no discarded output, no run log, and no timestamp field exists in any attached artifact, so the '95/115 L2 records present' detail and the claim that no verdict was recorded from it can be neither confirmed nor contradicted by me. What I can confirm is the state the disclosure implies for the final run: p5-L0.jsonl and p5-L2.jsonl each hold exactly 115 unique ids covering the full question set. I also confirm the disclosure's self-criticism is accurate — adjudicate_c36.py asserts equal L0/L2 denominators for localization but applies no completeness assertion to the P5 denominators, so it would have silently produced a P5 number from 95 records.

Two accepted questions (q105, q106) share the identical gold string 'Claude Code 2.1.220' while pointing at different gold documents. This does not violate the failable-multidoc gate as implemented (that gate counts occurrences across corpus bodies, at most 2), but it means a correct answer for one is a correct answer for the other, so the scoring rule cannot distinguish which document was reached for those two items. Effect on the reported numbers is at most 2/115 and does not move any threshold.

The L2 hit lists are not reconstructible from the L0 and L1 hit lists in the records. Only 22/115 L2 lists are subsets of L0 union L1 (top-8 truncated), and RRF(k=60) recomputed over the truncated legs reproduces the L2 set for 0/115 questions. This is expected if the navigator fuses full ranked lists internally and only the top-8 of each leg was recorded, so it is not evidence of an error — but it does mean the fusion arm, the study's primary arm, cannot be audited against its own legs from the shipped records. The retirement of RRF is therefore adjudicated on outcome only, with the mechanism unverifiable from the artifacts. I note the records are internally coherent on the point that matters: there is no question where the gold sits in both legs' top-8 yet is missing from the fused top-8.
